rationale: Evidence across independent cohorts demonstrates that dark-adapted (DA) full-field ERG in CLN3 disease presents with either an electronegative waveform (selective loss of b-wave relative to a-wave) or complete extinction/undetectability (as progressive a-wave loss supervenes). Sakti et al. (2023) observed electronegative ERGs in 5 of 5 patients presenting early (median age 6.2 years). However, Wright et al. (2020) demonstrated that only 4 of 8 (50%) CLN3 patients exhibited an electronegative ERG, whereas the other 4 (50%) had completely undetectable ERG responses due to advanced rod photoreceptor loss. Furthermore, Kuper et al. (2021) directly compared CLN3 patients (n=18) to early-onset Stargardt disease (STGD1, n=20) and confirmed that DA ERG responses in CLN3 were either absent or electronegative, whereas STGD1 patients typically had unaffected DA ERGs and never showed electronegative waveforms. Consequently, relying strictly on an electronegative ERG criterion yields false negatives in older or more advanced CLN3 presentations, whereas a composite criterion ('dark-adapted electronegative OR extinguished response') captures both stages while cleanly discriminating CLN3 from early-onset STGD1.

evidence.text: In a cohort comparing 18 CLN3 disease patients to 20 early-onset STGD1 patients presenting with visual loss at 5-10 years, dark-adapted full-field ERG responses were either absent or electronegative in CLN3 disease, whereas DA ERG responses in STGD1 were generally unaffected and none exhibited an electronegative ERG.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact age window or visual acuity threshold during which CLN3 disease transitions from an electronegative dark-adapted ERG to an undetectable ERG?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the chronological and functional inflection point will allow clinicians to know whether an extinguished ERG reflects late-stage presentation of CLN3 versus an alternate early-onset panretinal dystrophy.

new_directions.question_text: Does peripheral lymphocyte vacuole screening in conjunction with composite DA-ERG improve the diagnostic lead time for CLN3 over electrophysiology alone?
new_directions.rationale: Wright et al. found peripheral vacuolated lymphocytes in 8 of 8 CLN3 patients, suggesting a non-invasive, low-cost screening tool that can prevent misattribution when ERG is already completely extinguished.
